An architecture that defines the flow of sub-Business Processes and Business Activities that makes up a Business Process

The usage of a Business Process as a step in the flow of another Business Process

Usage of Business Events in Business Process Flow. These can either be initiating events or raised events in the process.
Usage of Business Event as an event that initiates a Business Process.
Usage of Business Event as an event that is raised by a Business Process.
Represents any event that occurs between an initiating and raised event
Used to capture a decision point in a Business Process Flow
Represents a logical Business Role participating in a Business Process
Represents an Information View that is processed in a Business Process Flow
Represents a logical Business Role conducting other Business Roles in a Business Process
An architecture that defines the sequence of Business Tasks that make up a Business Activity.

The usage of a Business Task in a Business Activity flow.
The starting point for a business activity flow

Usage of Business Events in Business Activity Flow. These can either be initiating events or raised events in the activity.
Usage of Business Event as an event that initiates a Business Activity.
Usage of Business Event as an event that is raised by a Business Activity.
An architecture model that defines static dependencies between Product Types (including information views that are required)
Super class of the usages that appear in a Static Product Type Architecture. Convenience super class to support use of the Protege Graph Widget.
The usage of a Product Type in a Static Product Type Architecture
An architecture model that defines static dependencies between Product (including information representations that are required)

The elements that can be contained within a Business Model Configuration Architecture
A usage of a Business Reference Architecture in a Business Model Configuration
A usage of an Application Reference Implementation in a Business Model Configuration

Class to capture types of products that are produced by the enterprise. Product Types are realisations of Product Concepts, and group the actual, physical products by type. E.g. in the motor manufacturer example, product types would be 'Car', 'Truck' as realisations of the 'Vehicle' concept. As a further example, a service company would define the types of a particular service (e.g. financial services) that they provide.
Class to manage the definition of business rules.

Class to capture the products that are produced by the enterprise. Products are instances of Product Types. E.g. in the motor manufacturer example, products could be 'Focus', 'Mustang' as instances of the 'Car' type. Equally, a service company would capture the service offerings.
A brand is a symbol by which a customer identifies market facing identifier that has a consistent set of principals for creating Customer Value Propositions that satisfy a particular set of needs
It is the medium for the customer to interact with the organisation to obtain or access products, features and market services
Features are components or characteristics of the product and services we make available to customers
Specific implementations of components or characteristics of products (or services) that are made available to customers

Used to group business processes, activities or tasks that are variants of each other into a single 'family', allowing them to be distinct while at the same time ceonvetying that they are related.\nThis provides a more powerful and flexible approach than using Enumerations or Taxonomies as it allows contextual information to be added, for example, Business Process X is a standard for the EMEA region within its Business Process family
Represents a customer persona's typical experience over time when engaging with an enterprise
Represents a key touchpoint in a Customer Journey between a customer persona and an enterprise
Class to manage the definition of Business Conditions that determine whether a process can begin, or can be completed
Defines a configurations of enterprise elements that are required to deliver a business model in a specific context
A high-level categorical classification of Product (or Service) consumers
The Physical view of the Business Layer of the meta model. A set of meta-classes that help to describes the physical implementation of the business - the WHERE and WHOM.

A specific, named, group, team or individual that peforms a role in a process.\nActors are used to capture how the enterprise is actually organised, in terms of the real companies, divisions, teams and individuals that make up the organisation. Actors take on the Roles (defined in the organisation design) to execute Physical processes/activities.
An individual person that performs a physical business process type
A position within an organisation (Group Actor) which is filled by an individual actor
Represents an archetype of customer groups that engage with an enterprise
An iorganisation or team that performs a physical business process type
A specific (and named) physical location where processes or activities take place.
Base class for the Physical Business Process meta classes. Holds basic information and the relation to Application Providers and Application Function Implementations that support this process.
An instance of a Business Process that is performed by a group or individual in the enterprise.
An instance of a Business Activity that is performed by a group or individual in the enterprise.
Represents a predicted or actual occurrence of a business event
Represents a predicted or actual business event that occurs outside of the enterprise
Base class for Application Architecture constructs. All the meta classes for the Application Layer are sub-classes of this.

The Conceptual view of the Application Layer of the meta model. A set of meta-classes that helps to describe the capabilities or requirements for the behaviour and functionality of the IT business systems of the enterprise
High level rules that govern the manner in which application capabilities are implemented by the enterprise

Provides the abstract perspective on the functional behaviour required to support the business. Capabilities are mapped to the Business Domain that they support.\nOne of the additional purposes of this meta class is to provide a grounding for Applications Functions, enabling one to model that a particular Application Function \\\\\\"is a one of these <Application Capabilities>\\\\\\"
Class to define and manage the internal and external influences that motivate the Application Objectives.
A strategic goal associated with the Application Architecture of the enterprise
Defines a high level aspiration for the application architecture

This is an optional top level (and least specific) construct in the Application Architecture. It provides a means of categorising Application Capabilities independently of the business context in which they are required

The Logical view of the Application Layer of the meta model. A set of meta-classes that helps to describes the logical design of the functionality and behaviour of the IT systems that support the business

A well-defined component of functional behaviour that provides a logical grouping of related Application Functions. e.g. ExchangeRates Service, CreditCardPayment Service or logical application such as CRM System, ERP System. The specification of the service - in terms of what it does - is defined by the set of Application Functions that it provides.
An Application Service that is made up of one or more Application Services
A discrete piece of functional behaviour that an application provides. e.g. GetAllExchangeRates, MakeCreditCardPayment

A convenience component for defining types of applications. Enables the application modeller to specify that 2 Application Providers are each a type of an Application. e.g. applicationProviderX and applicationProviderY are types of SAP (Application). In addition, this can be used to group Application Providers under a name by which they are commonly referred to in the enterprise.

Base class of Application Provider and Application Function Implementations. These are logical things that provide implementations to the Application Services and Application Functions. These are real application components that one can buy (e.g. packaged applications) or that have been built - either customised packages or purely bespoke applications.

An Application Provider provides one or more Application Services. To provide a service, the Application Provider should provide - through its Application Function Implementations - all of the Application Functions of the Application Service that this Application Provider provides. e.g. a specific implementation of SAP R/3 - the ERP System, the Finance System, Cast Iron Expenses project.
An Application Provider that is made up of one or more Application Providers

Represents a n application component that is solely responsible for acting as an interface between two or more other applications, e.g. a Native API, an Application Integration Flow, an Application Integration Sub-Component

An implementation of an Application Function provided by an application - whether bespoke or packaged. e.g. a doCreditCardPayment transaction in SAP Finance implements a MakeCreditCardPayment Application Function.
A discrete software component that is contained within the logical software architecture of an Application Provider
Class of elements describing events that occur in the application layer.
Class to represent System Events that are raised by schedules or are timed events
Class to represent System Events that are raised by parties external to the enterprise.
A model that describes relationships between logical application elements
The architecture describing the sub components of an Application Service - a STATIC view and static dependencies between them.
Super class of components that participate in service-based Application Architecture models
The usage of an Application Function in an Application Service Architecture.
The usage of an Application Service in an Application Service Architecture. This is used in both the Static and Dynamic Application Service Architectures so has slots for its use in either.
Usage of Business Events in an Application Service Architecture. These can either be initiating events or raised events in the architecture.
Usage of Business Event as an event that initiates an Application Service.
Usage of Business Event as an event that is raised by an Application Service.

An Architecture defining the dynamic nature of an Application Function. The architecture describes the sub-components (Application Services and Application Functions) and the relationships between those sub components.
The architecture describing the sub components of an Application Provider - a STATIC view.
The type of classes contained within a static application provider architecture
A usage of an application provider in a static application provider architecture
The usage of an Application Function Implementation in a Static Application Provider Archictecture.

Architecture defining the dynamic behaviour of the implementation of a function implementation. This architecture defines how the Application Providers that are used in the architecture interact (by requesting Function Implementations) in order to deliver the behaviour of the Function Implementation.
Super class of components that are used to define a dynamic view of the relationships between Application Function Implementations and Application Providers.
The usage of an Application Function Implementation in a Dyanmic Application Provider archictecture.
The usage of an Application Provider in an Application Provider Architecture.
Usage of System Events in an Dynamic Application Provider Architecture. These can either be initiating events or raised events in the architecture.
Usage of System Event as an event that initiates an Application Provider or Function Implementation.
Usage of System Event as an event that is raised by an Application Provider or Function Implementation.
A high level logical software architecture model for an Application Provider, comprised of Software Component Usages, Information Representations and their relationships
The classes that are contained within a Logical Software Architecture model
A usage of a Software Component
The usage of an Information Representation in a Logical Software Architecture.
Represents an Application Provider's ability to provide a specific Application Service
A meta-class that helps to describes the physical implementation of the enterprise's IT applications

A physical deployment of an Application component in the organisation. e.g. the Production Environment, the Test Environment etc. Deployments define one or more instances of the application (e.g. live, failover) to capture all the physical instances of the Application.
A convenience construct for working with multiple (typically large numbers) instances of Application Deployments. E.g. several hundred deployments of the standard desktop application build.
Base class for Information Architecture constructs. All the meta classes for the Information Layer are sub-classes of this.
The Conceptual view of the Information Layer of the meta model. A set of meta-classes that helps to describe the information concepts supporting the business
High level rules that govern the manner in which information assets are created and managed by the enterprise
High level, conceptual elements that capture the type of Information items that are used in the course of running the business. e.g. Cost, Production Order, Sales Volume.
Class to capture data subjects in the Information Layer. Data Subjects define the 'types' of Data used in the enterprise and provide the semantic grounding for Data Objects.
Class to define and manage the internal and external influences that motivate the Information Objectives.
A strategic goal associated with the Information Architecture of the enterprise
Defines a high level aspiration for the information architecture
This is the top level (and least specific) construct in the Information Architecture. It provides a means of categorising Information Concepts independently of the context in which they are used
A word or phrase that describes a concept that is used by the business
This is an optional top level (and least specific) construct in the Data Architecture. It provides a means of categorising Data Subjects independently of the context in which they are used
The Logical view of the Application Layer of the meta model. A set of meta-classes that helps to describe the logical design of the information and data that support the business.
A model that describes relationships to and from logical information elements
Super class of components that participate in logical architecture models
The usage of an Information View as either an input to an Application Function OR as an output of an Application Function. The view can be used as one or the other.
DEPRECATED in version 1.0.\nThe usage of an Information Representation in an architecture.
Class to capture the most basic types of data that act as building blocks for Data Attributes (e.g. integer, string, float, date)
Base class of Data Objects and Data Object Attributes.

Class to capture and manage Data Objects used by systems to provide Information to the applications and processes. Data Objects provide a logical grouping of Data Attributes and realise conceptual Data Subjects.
Describes an individual attribute of data. Data Attributes are used and grouped, logically, by Data Objects.

Base class of Data Representations and Data Representation Attributes. These are logical aspects of data that provide implementations of Data Objects and Data Object Attributes and are specific to the applications that manage them.
A specific representation of a Data Object, for example MAT_MAS, which is SAP's representation of a Product Item.
A particular attribute or item of a Data_Representation

A refined view of an Information Concept that can also include the relevant attributes of the view, if required (e.g. to show how one View of a Concept differs from another). An Information View describes in more detail a certain view of a Concept, e.g. Cost per Product for Site.
A particular attribute or item of information that is used or shared in the definition of Information Views

A specific representation of an Information View using a specific technology. Example technologies would include XML schema, a relational database schema and can also include things like paper forms. The relationship to the Technology layer is to a Technology Product Role, which defines how a Technology Product is being used, e.g. Oracle RDBMS, ebXML schema.
A particular attribute or item of information that is used or shared in the definition of Information Representation
The Physical view of the Application Layer of the meta model. A set of meta-classes that helps to describes the physical deployment of the enterprise's information assets

A physical deployment of an Information Representation where that information is being stored. The Information Store is defined by the deployment role that it takes, e.g. Production, Development, Test. Instances of the Information Store are managed as Information Store Instances (see Technology Physical->Technology Instance for more details about Information Store Instances)
A convenience class for representing a group of multiple deployments of an Information Store, e.g. deployments to a production desktop environment on 100 desktop machines
A model that describes relationships to and from physical information elements
Super class of components that participate in phsyical architecture models
Represents the physical data stored in an Information Store
Base class for Technology Architecture constructs. All the meta classes for the Technology Layer are sub-classes of this.
The Conceptual view of the Technology Layer of the meta model. A set of meta-classes that helps to describe the capabilities or requirements for the technology infrastructure of the enterprise
High level rules that govern the manner in which technology capabilities are implemented in the enterprise
Provides a means of categorising technology capabilities and defining technology areas.

Technology Capabilities are conceptual constructs that describe WHAT a piece of technology does or needs to do.\nThe contained technologies slot is used as part of a DEFINITION of a Capability to describe Capabilities that are considered to be part of (contained in - as opposed to used to deliver) a larger Capability. To DESIGN how a new Capability could delivered by using existing Capabilities, a Technology Capability Architecture is used to describe the new Capability.
A model that describes relationships to and from technology capabilities
The Technology Capability Architecture is used to DESIGN how a new Capability could delivered by using existing Capabilities. E.g., to define conceptual technology models.
Super class of components that participate in Conceptual Technology Architecture models
The use of a Technology Capability in the context of a Technology Capability Architecture or Conceptual Technology Model.

Technology Function Types define, at a finer level of granularity, what technical functions a capability offers. The Function Types provide a grounding for the Functions defined in Technology Components.
Class to define and manage the internal and external influences that motivate the Technology Objectives.
A strategic goal associated with the Technology Architecture of the enterprise
Defines a high level aspiration for the technology architecture
The Logical view of the Technology Layer of the meta model. A set of meta-classes that helps to describes the logical design of the enterprise's technology infrastructure

Class to capture logical types - or classes - of Technology that are used to provide Technology Capabilities. e.g. Application Server, Message Oriented Middleware, Operating System. These should be real types of technology that are available today (or are state of the art) but not actual products.

Technology Composites are Technology Components that are made up of other Technology Components and have a defining architecture which describes the Technology Components that are used to make the composite.

own_slot_value.value: Technology Function define, at a finer level of granularity, what technical functions a component offers. e.g. a relational database might offer create(), update(), read(), delete()

Base class of actual technology products and builds of products that are used to deliver technology infrastructure for IT systems. Technology Providers are used to provide Technology Components (which are higher level logical constructs) in the architecture.

A Technology Provider that is specific to a particular organisation. This may have been built in-house or be a specific architecture of Technology Providers, assembled to provide the specified Technology Component.

Architecture to describe the make-up of a Technology Product Build, in terms of the Technology Products and the relationships between them that make up the build.

Architecture that describes the make up of a Technology Product.
Set of allowable classes that appear in Technology Product Architectures.

Usage of the specified Protocol by Product Usages in an architecture.
Class to define dependencies of a Technology Product in terms of supported and un-supported products.

Class to group related Technology Product instances into a product 'family'. This provides a more powerful and flexible approach than using Enumerations or Taxonomies. Each version instance can be related in terms of the supersession of versions using the supersedes_version slot. e.g. ProductX 2.0 supersedes ProductX 1.5
The Logical view of the Technology Layer of the meta model. A set of meta-classes that helps to describes the physical implementation of the enterprise's technology infrastructure
An instance of a piece of hardware or software technology in the infrastructure of the organisation. (e.g. a specific server or a specific instance of an installed piece of software).
Class to capture hardware Technology Instances, e.g. servers, desktop workstations, network routers and so on.

Class to capture software Technology Instances deployed to a particular Technology Node. Infrastructure Software is all software that does not directly encode application functionality, e.g. operating systems, middleware (including Application Servers and integration software), RDBMS software, virtual machines and so on.

Class to represent instances of the applications software that are deployed to a particular Technology Node. Application software is software code or configuration that encodes application functionality, e.g. Java EAR or WAR, or an executable application program file.
An instance of an Information Store that has been deployed to a physical node.
A locate-able Node in the infrastructure on which other Nodes and Technology Instances are deployed.

The base class for meta classes that operate on the core Business, Application, Information and Technology layers providing EA supporting capabilities, e.g. Strategy Management, Security, Programme Management, Information Lifecycle Management
Category for classes that support the definition and maintenance of strategy across the architecture layers

An Architecture State groups a set of related architectures in a particular context or configuration. Such contexts could be temporal, e.g. reflecting architectures that are valid today or in the future. Equally, this context could represent the set of architectures required to achieve a particular goal. Naming of Architecture States is important. Architecture States should be named for the configuration of architectures that they group. What does this state do for the organisation? Avoid names such as 'Current State' or 'Future State' as these Architecture States can be used in different contexts.

Describes the strategic plan of action for a given architecture element. This is an abstract class that provides an anchor for specific strategic plan sub-classes that are themselves associated with specific Architecture elements to meet an organisation's specific modelling requirements
A Strategic plan for elements in the Business Layer of the architecture
A Strategic plan for elements in the Application Layer of the architecture
A Strategic plan for elements in the Information Layer of the architecture
A Strategic plan for elements in the Technology Layer of the architecture
Strategic Plan for elements that managed in the Security Management section of the meta model.

The Open Source Initiative (OSI) is a non-profit corporation formed to educate about and advocate for the benefits of open source and to build bridges among different constituencies in the open-source community. One of their most important activities is as a standards body, maintaining the Open Source Definition for the good of the community. The Open Source Initiative Approved License trademark and program creates a nexus of trust around which developers, users, corporations and governments can organize open-source cooperation.

The Free Software Foundation (FSF) is a 501(c)3 donor supported charity founded in 1985 and based in Boston, MA, USA. The FSF has a worldwide mission to promote computer user freedom and to defend the rights of all free software users.
A Per CPU license model is used for software licenses where the number of units is calculated by the number of processors in all the machines that make up the software runtime platform.
A Per Core license model is used for software licenses where the number of units is calculated by the number of processor cores in all the machines that make up the software runtime platform.
A Per User license model is used where each user of the product must each have a license to use it.
An Enterprise license model grants an organisation freedom to use a product in what ever number of units are required.
A commercial license is a type of license where commercial terms, e.g. a fee, must be paid in order for the license to be granted.

Open source licenses oblige the owner of the product to make the details of how it was constructed available to the users of that product. Users are free to build upon the product to tailor it to their requirements or to build upon it to make a new product.

A subscription license is a type of license where commercial terms, e.g. a recurring fee, must be paid in order for the license to be granted and these terms must continue to be met in for the license to remain granted.

The Essential Project is a set of open source, enterprise architecture support tools developed to be used with a variety of EA approaches and frameworks. 'Essential' because these tools are focused on providing capabilities that are essential to maximising the value of enterprise architecture; helping organisations manage and analyse the knowledge needed to make decisions that impact or are impacted by the enterprise architecture.

A network switch is a broad and imprecise marketing term for a computer networking device that connects network segments. The term commonly refers to a Network bridge that processes and routes data at the Data link layer (layer 2) of the OSI model. Switches that additionally process data at the Network layer (layer 3 and above) are often referred to as Layer 3 switches or Multilayer switches. The term Network switch does not generally encompass unintelligent or passive network devices such as hubs and repeaters.
